medium.syllabus_scope: First 50% of the ordered syllabus, primarily Unit 1: Constitution-making, Preamble, basic structure, features, Fundamental Rights/Duties, Articles 14/19/21 and Directive Principles.

Questions: A citizen damages public property during a protest. Which Fundamental Duty is most directly relevant to the conduct?
A state policy seeks environmental improvement, but an official arbitrarily denies access to a public benefit. What is a balanced analysis?

A constitutional amendment changes the composition of a body, and challengers claim the change damages separation of powers and judicial review. What evidence is most important to the basic-structure question?
Who chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
A Fundamental Right is asserted against a policy goal in Part IV. Which reading method best reflects the constitutional relationship?
A citizen's speech is restricted by a law. Which is the most accurate way to evaluate the restriction under Article 19?
India is described in the Preamble as a:
A student says that because the Constitution is written, every rule must appear in one unamended original document. Which correction is best?

A citizen challenges an order affecting personal liberty. The authority claims Article 21 only applies when a law is completely absent, not when procedure exists but is arbitrary. Which response best reflects modern constitutional reasoning at course level?
Who is the constitutional head of a state in India?
A claimant argues that because a policy appears in Part IV, courts must enforce it as if it were a Fundamental Right. Which constitutional text most directly challenges that claim?
A government scheme promotes social welfare, but its implementation treats similarly situated citizens arbitrarily. Which constitutional analysis is strongest?
Which part opens the Constitution of India and states its guiding ideals?

An amendment changes an institution in a way alleged to eliminate judicial review and constitutional limits. Which framework most directly addresses whether a constitutional amendment can destroy foundational features?
A public authority refuses the same legal protection to two people in materially identical circumstances without a relevant reason. Which constitutional principle is most directly raised?
A student argues that the Preamble itself grants an unlimited legal power to an executive agency. What is the key flaw?
An official says Article 14 guarantees identical treatment even where relevant circumstances differ. Which statement is more accurate?
A teacher is describing an amendment's constitutional history. Which pair is correct?
Which Article protects specified freedoms, subject to constitutional restrictions?
A person says all Directive Principles are individually enforceable in court because they are 'fundamental in governance'. Which reasoning corrects the conflation?
A school textbook says Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution through an amendment. Which pairing is correct?
Which Article guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws?
When did the Constitution of India come into force?
The Constitution's Preamble is invoked to interpret an ambiguous provision. Which description best fits its role?
A new state policy is consistent with a Directive Principle but is implemented in a way that violates Article 21. What follows?
What is the principal purpose of a constitution?
A Fundamental Duty to protect the environment is cited to automatically deny a person's otherwise lawful speech. Which conclusion is most careful?
Which Article protects life and personal liberty?
Fundamental Rights are primarily contained in which Part of the Constitution?
A law restricts a citizen's speech to address a public concern. The citizen argues Article 19 makes all restrictions invalid. Which reasoning is most defensible?

medium.syllabus_scope: Full syllabus practice bank for Mid 2; Mid 1 is the only exam constrained to the first half.

Questions: A student confuses the Chief Election Commissioner with the State Election Commissioner. Which distinction is most accurate?
A policy objective appears in Part IV, but a petitioner wants a court order solely to enforce it as a Directive Principle. Which constitutional statement is most relevant?
An official detains a person and relies only on a personal preference, without lawful authority or procedure. Which provision is most directly engaged?
A citizen damages public property during a protest. Which Fundamental Duty is most directly relevant to the conduct?
The Prime Minister's Council of Ministers loses a confidence vote in Lok Sabha. Which constitutional principle is most directly implicated?
A policy objective is listed as a Directive Principle and is consistent with a Fundamental Right. Which approach best reflects the Constitution's framework?
A person argues that a Fundamental Right can never be limited. Which response best fits the course topics?
An amendment changes a constitutional provision but is challenged for damaging the Constitution's basic structure. Which doctrine is most relevant?
A bill concerning ordinary Union governance is being studied. Which distinction between Parliament and the executive is correct?
A parent or guardian is asked which Fundamental Duty concerns children's education. Which is accurate?
A general election to the Lok Sabha is being conducted, and a separate city municipal election is scheduled. Which bodies have the respective constitutional roles?
A policy proposal concerns village-level elected self-government. Which amendment is most directly connected with the Panchayat framework?
A legal complaint concerns both an arbitrary procedure affecting liberty and unequal treatment under law. Which Articles are most directly relevant?
A student says Fundamental Duties and Fundamental Rights are identical because both appear in the Constitution. Which correction is strongest?
An amendment is challenged as destroying a foundational feature such as constitutional supremacy. Which case-law doctrine is relevant to the course's basic-structure topic?
Which statement best describes the ECI's constitutional role?
A public authority refuses the same legal protection to two people in materially identical circumstances without a relevant reason. Which constitutional principle is most directly raised?
A Governor receives advice from a state's Council of Ministers for ordinary state executive business. Which official is the normal political head of that Council?

A district administration office is implementing state policy and coordinating local public services. Which level is most directly represented?

A state makes policy to improve public health and welfare. Which constitutional part is especially relevant as guiding principles for State policy?

A municipality's constitutional framework is being discussed. Which Part was added for urban local bodies by the 74th Amendment?
A State Election Commission plans local-body elections, but a student says Article 324 alone assigns the ECI all elections of every kind. Which correction is best?
A public authority treats people unequally and also restricts a citizen's speech. Which two provisions are the most direct starting points for analysis?
A local body has been asked to handle city-level services rather than district rural planning. Which institution is a better fit?
A citizen's speech is restricted by a law. Which is the most accurate way to evaluate the restriction under Article 19?
A government policy promotes public health but a person argues it is a Directive Principle. Which statement best distinguishes its legal status from a Fundamental Right?
